1. Introduction
The Sepehr-Jufair Field is located in the Abadan Plain, Southwest of Khuzestan Province, about 60 km
West of Ahwaz and 30 km South of Susangerd. The Sepehr-Jufair field covers about 352 square
kilometers area with approximately 23 kilometers long and 27 kilometers wide. Figure-1 illustrates the
geographical situation of the Sepehr and Jufair gentle culminations that are located in the vicinity of
South Azadegan and Yadavaran giant fields. Currently four wells are in production in the Jufair area.
The penetrated formations from top to bottom will be Aghajari, Mishan, Gachsaran, Asmari, Pabdeh,
Gurpi, Ilam respectively.

                               Figure 1-1: Geographical location of the Sepehr-Jufair field

The first well (JR-01) was Spudded in the crestal area of the Jufair Field by DEMINEX Co. in 1975. The
first drilling operation was continued to the depth of 4276 meters (MD) in order to evaluate the
Bangestan (Ilam and Sarvak) and Gadvan reservoir layers. After drilling the well, five wells have been
drilled in the Jufair area. Based on the achieved data from these wells, it was planned to drill Well JR-
06 (as an appraisal/ producer well) to further investigate the Khami Group layers, especially the Lower
Fahliyan reservoir layer. Well JR-06 was drilled as an appraisal/production well at December 2020 in
vicinity of Ilam horizontal well. The evaluation of acquired data from this well proved having good
potential of hydrocarbon in the Jufair area. In order to further investigation of Khami Group it was
decided to drill new appraisal/production wells in Jufair area. The third production well which is
named Ilam horizontal well will be drilled in central part of Sepehr-Jufair Field in vicinity of the Well
JR-06 & JR-05. Geographically, the well JR-09 will be spudded in vicinity of the well JR-05 with a
distance about 1616m. Therefore, the aforementioned well was used as reference well. In fact, the
well JR-09 will be drilled in Western Area of Jufair Culmination, in the West of well JR-05. The Ilam
horizontal well will be drilled into the Ilam Formation (2962 TVDSS/4126 mMD depth).

2.5. Well Objective:
•   Zero safety incidents

    Achieve all safety, environment and community related objectives.
•   Deliver Ilam New Well JR-09 as Ilam Horizontal Production well that is effectively hydraulically

    isolated by achieving zonal isolation requirements to secure the well for drilling horizontal section

   and production through the reservoir in the 6 1/8" & 5 7/8" section.
•   Hit all subsurface targets within allowable range.
•   Obtain open hole wireline logs and cuttings sample to evaluate the reservoir quality of the Ilam

    formation. Also provide appropriate information on non-target reservoir interval.
•   Collect data for drilling performance optimization and future well planning.
•  Adopt best drilling practices in order to have quality borehole across Ilam formation.
•   Successful well handover as per plan.

The drilling program is a guideline to conduct drilling operation. The drilling team may adjust
appropriate changes according to site condition, but any changes must be approved by Pasargad
E&P Company.

2.6. New Well Program Generation:
•  PECO Drilling Engineer is responsible for preparing the drilling program which is issued for every

    well drilled.
•  The program has been reviewed/Approved by Pasargad E&P Company.
•  Programs occasionally may change with potential improvements. For this reason, program

   amendments shall be issued under the Company Management of Change (MOC) procedure.
•  Programs shall be followed unless an amendment is approved by Pasargad E&P Company.
•  Programs shall be distributed as per approved distribution list.
•  Any team member who sees a potential problem or improvement can and should suggest an

   amendment.
•   All significant changes to the program will be done after written MOC approved by Pasargad E&P

   Company. These program changes must be documented and then sent through the program

    approval process.

2.7. JR-09 Operation Summary:

JR-09 is horizontal production well with expected TD of 4126mMD. The target formation is Ilam
formation.
    ▪    Drill 12 1/4" vertical hole to ±2400 m MD (KOP)

    ▪    Drill 12 ¼” directional hole to ±2639m MD

    ▪    Drill 8 ½” directional hole to ±3073m MD

    ▪    Drill 6 1/8” main horizontal open hole to ±4126m MD

    ▪    Drill 5 7/8" Lateral leg from previous 6 1/8" open hole (from 3500m) with 500m length to TD

    ▪  RIH Kick off string including suitable tubing hanger and temporary X-mass tree

    ▪  Perform selective acidizing by inflatable packer and perform flow test

    ▪  Run slotted liner as per wellbore stability condition of 6 1/8" main hole (as contingency)

    ▪  R/U Perforation equipment and perform perforation in Ilam 2A layer

    ▪   Displace the well by CaCl2 completion fluid

    ▪  Run ESP completion

    ▪  Flow the Well and Record Data

   ▪  Secure the Well and Release the Rig

3. Geological Information
Well JR-09 will be spudded as a producer well and adjacent to Wells JR‐03, JR‐04 and JR-05 in the
North West part of Sepehr-Jufair Field. This Well will be penetrated finally into the Ilam reservoir layers
with estimated depth of ±4126mMD (2980mTVD).

In terms of structural geology, the proposed well is located in the Western part of the Jufair
culmination. It is noted that the new updating Ilam‐Main depth map has been used in order to
determine the accurate position of the Ilam horizontal well. (Figure 3-1)

                        Figure 3-1: Sepehr-Jufair structural geometries based on Ilam depth maps

A brief description of the predicted stratigraphy column in the well JR-09 from top to TD are as follows:

3.1. Aghajari Formation (from surface to 1408 m MD)
This huge clastic/marly succession (1408 m thickness) is Pliocene-Pleistocene in age and mostly
composed of red marls, interbedded sandstone, gypsum/anhydrite, and red claystone layers. It is
expected that the claystone and anhydrite intervals increase from top to the bottom. The clastic
intervals include of sandstone and siltstone layers are variably consolidated and generally described

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                  Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production
                             Operations Project

                                  Well Drilling Program - JR-09

  Doc. No:            SJD4   DDRGED   DRDR    PLDR     9001     D01       Page 27 of 281

as light brown and light gray colors, fine to medium sand grains. They are commonly well sorted
representing sub‐angular to subrounded sand grains. The main body of sandstone packages are loose
(un‐consolidated sands), friable to moderately hard. The mentioned interbedded marls are red to
reddish brown color, generally sticky and slightly silty, soft to firm and grading to claystone. The
claystone layers are reddish in color, showing generally soft, sticky, and amorphous. They are locally
calcareous, grading to gray marl, generally non‐silty and occasionally mottled. There are negligible
argillaceous limestone beds that can be observed in both middle and lower parts of the Aghajari
formation (between depths of 600 to 800 m). Both 32” and 24” holes will be drilled into the Aghajari
formation and 26” and 18 5/8” casings will be run within the formation. In addition, 26” casing shoe
will be set at the near top of this clastic formation, about the depth of 100m (MD).

3.2. Mishan Formation (from 1408 to 1496m MD)
The Mishan formation (about 88 meters thick) with Middle Miocene in age, is mainly comprised of
alternated marl, anhydrite and limestone beds in this well, overlying the topmost Gachsaran anhydrite
layer. 24” Hole size will be penetrated within this small marly/ carbonate formation.

3.3. Gachsaran Formation (from 1496 to 2020m MD)
The Gachsaran formation is Early to Middle Pliocene in age, and expected to be about 524 m thick. It
is predominantly comprised  of evaporate successions (Anhydrite and  salt beds), which are
interbedded with some gray to red marls. In terms of drilling hazards, the Gachsaran formation is
subdivided into two (2) major intervals, called Upper and Lower Gachsaran. The Upper Gachsaran
corresponds to members 2 to 7, predominantly constituted by alternated anhydrite, marly and salt
successions. The marl is gray to light gray in color and soft, which is seen commonly interbedded by
white anhydrite layers. The relevant anhydrite is white to milky in color, soft, partly crystalline,
medium hard to hard in terms of physical properties.

The Lower Gachsaran interval, usually corresponds to member 1 (Cap Rock unit) known as alternated
salt and anhydrite beds (in form of hard and crystalline). The basal part of Gachsaran formation is
characterized by dark grey to grey marls, thin salt beds and interbedded anhydrite layers.

The top of Gachsaran formation will be drilled by 24” hole and 18 5/8” casing shoe will be set around
10 to 30m inside this formation, the rest of Gachsaran formation will be drilled by 17 1/2” hole size to
set 13 3/8” casing shoe inside Cap rock unit (8-10 m inside Cap Rock). The rest of Gachsaran interval
will be drilled by 12 1/4” bit size.

3.4. Asmari Formation (from 2020 to 2401.5 m MD)
The Oligocene‐Miocene Asmari formation (About 381.5 m thickness) to be subdivided into
several distinct stratigraphical units in this well.  It  is predicted that the top of Asmari
formation is made by limestone and interbedded carbonate succession (Less than 25 m).
Whilst,  the  upper  part   is  mostly  dominated  by   clastic  packages   including
sandstones/siltstones beds (About 150 m thickness). The above‐mentioned sandy interval
shows some interbedded gray marls, few dolomites and scattered brownish claystone layers.
The relevant gray to light gray sandstones is essentially medium sorted, medium to coarse

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                  Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production
                             Operations Project

                                  Well Drilling Program - JR-09

  Doc. No:            SJD4   DDRGED   DRDR    PLDR     9001     D01       Page 28 of 281

grain size and contain some ironic oxides such as pyrite. The interbedded claystone package
is characterized by reddish to light brown color, soft and sticky form. The lower part of Asmari
formation is again carbonated (About 75 m thickness) and essentially composed of light
gray/gray dolomitic limestone to dolomite beds. The base of  this formation  is also
characterized by thin layer sandstones that are directly located on the marly facies of the
Pabdeh formation. Asmari formation will be drilled by 12 ¼” hole in Ilam new well.

3.5. Pabdeh Formation (from 2401.5 to 2651.5m MD)
Pabdeh formation (Paleocene‐Eocene age) is estimated to be about 245.5 m thick, in this well.
This formation is expected to be subdivided into two (2) lithological units as well. The upper
part consists of grey to dark‐brown argillaceous limestone and Limestone, accompanied with
some interbedded marls and shale/ claystone. In terms of microfossil contents planktonic
microfauna is dominant throughout the Pabdeh argillaceous intervals. This formation is
mainly consisting of light grey, pale yellowish brown and rarely off-white moderate hard to
hard argillaceous limestone with chert nodules (approximately 30% in 60-80 m interval).
There are some interlayers of dark-brown argillaceous limestone beds. The 12 1/4” hole will
be penetrated into this marly/ carbonate formation.
Note: In upper Pabdeh has water wet calaystone/Shale which can caved without sufficient
mud material (KCl).

3.6. Gurpi Formation (from 2651.5 to 2974m MD)
The Gurpi formation (Campanian to Maastrichtian age) is estimated to be about 267 m thick and is
also expected to be subdivided into three (3) stratigraphical units in this well, including Upper Gurpi,
Tarbur Tongue and Lower Gurpi from top to the bottom of the formation respectively. The Upper
Gurpi unit is mainly characterized by grey to dark‐brownish argillaceous limestone beds, which are
assigned by abundant planktonic microfauna and noticeable clay contents. This interval is mostly
composed of gray buff to gray, soft to medium hard, glauconitic to argillaceous limestone intervals
with interbedded grey marls.

The middle part of Gurpi formation corresponds to a shallow marine carbonate stack that named as
Tarbur Tongue. This particular carbonate interval was developed in the Sepehr‐Jufair area like other
areas of Abadan Plain, which is commonly characterized by bioclastic limestone facies and shows huge
accumulation of the large skeletal fragments such as bivalve debris. The Tarbur tongue is a cream to
light gray in color, illustrating weak to moderate reservoir quality (Estimated based on nearby wells)
and as with other parts of Abadan Plain, it also has economic oil-bearing intervals.

The Lower Gurpi unit is overlain directly by Tarbur limestone and shows so many similarities to the
Upper Gurpi unit in terms of lithology and facies. The Lower Gurpi is mainly characterized by grey color
argillaceous limestone facies (planktonic facies is dominant), which are interbedded by some grey
color marly intervals.

In terms of drilling hazards, these units have not shown any particular hazards until now. The 12 1/4”
and 8 ½” hole size will penetrate this marly/ carbonate formation.

────────────────────────────────────────────
                  Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production
                             Operations Project

3.7. Ilam Reservoir Formation (from 2974 to 4126m MD)
The Ilam formation (Santonian age), is expected to be drilled about 67 m thickness in this well, known
as one of the main oil-bearing reservoir formations, extended predominantly in the Operation Area.
Lithologically, the Ilam formation is essentially comprised of grey to brown limestone intervals,
observed often with few interbedded marly to claystone beds (Rarely pyritic).

Therefore, the upper part of Ilam formation is characterized by an alternation between limestone/
dolomitic limestone beds and marly to claystone interlayers. The Upper Ilam carbonate interval shows
fair reservoir quality in the Jufair area, accompanied with noticeable economic hydrocarbon volume
(It is highly recommended to check this interval accurately).

The main reservoir body of Ilam formation, named Ilam-Main unit, producing economic oil in this area
and essentially composed of mud-supported limestone facies with huge micro-porosity volumes. This
carbonate stack is characterized by planktonic microfossils such as Oligosteginid and Globotruncanid
families and accompanied with negligible clay contents.

The lower part, which named Ilam-Poor (In terms of low reservoir quality), corresponds to a small
muddy limestone interval, overlying directly the Laffan unit and represents negligible hydrocarbon
contents and mostly tightened or fully saturated by formation water. The main target of the Ilam wells
is to produce from Ilam-Main unit (Il-IIIB: 3070.5m MD (-2937m TVDSS)) and II-AII, so the lower part
of Ilam formation will not be penetrated. The 8 ½” hole sizes (As deviated well) and 6 1/8” (As
horizontal leg- Ilam-Main) will penetrate this marly/ carbonate formation.

3.10.4. Drilling Hazard in Nearby Wells
Over-Pressure

The formation pressure gradient in Gachsaran Formation reaches 152pcf based on the data of
offset wells (JR-02). Precautions should be taken to prevent any well kick. Enough weighting
material and kill mud must be stocked at rig site.

4.1. 17" Hole Section Potential Drilling Hazard

  Potential Hazard                          How to mitigate

                      Gachsaran formation consisting mainly of Anhydrate and Marls with inter beds of salt.

                      Gachsaran formation also consists of marly limestone. This is a potential salt water flow zone.
    Salt water flow     Maintain MW as plan MW.
                      Check Calcium ions while drilling, in case of showing increasing trend, drilling to be stopped.
                      Flow check if fast break experience.
                       Maintain MW as plan MW.
  Loss of circulation   Control running speed to prevent surge effect.
                         Control mud rheology.
                          Closely monitor losses while drilling.
                       Maintain MW as plan MW.
                       Minimize the overbalance (by decreasing mud weight)
   Stuck drill string
                       Minimize stationary time.
                         Increase drill collar and drill string stabilization.
                       Optimize fluid properties in attempts to minimize the risk of sticking.

                          Entire bit Balling risk will be reduced by consistently high flow rates, and good hole cleaning.
                       Ensure of pumping at high flow rates, and sufficient HSI (>2).
                     With tri-cone bits, center jet and oriented nozzle will also aid preventing balling (oriented nozzle
                           directs part of the flow onto the cutting structure).
                       Avoid excessive WOB while drilling through Gachsaran formation.
      Bit Balling
                         Actions once balling has been detected:
                        •    Bits can be cleared if balling is detected early enough and actions taken.
                        •   Reduce WOB when ROP drops, pick up bit off bottom as quickly as possible and increase flow
                                  rate.
                        •    Spin bit off bottom with high RPM and high flow rate for a period of time
                        •   Resume drilling with low weight
                        •   Prepare to pump pills (KCL solution pill), leave to soak and try to dissolve/loosen balled material

                     To minimize chances of stuck pipe, avoid pulling above 25 Klbs.
       Drill string        Inspect drill string regularly.
      corrosion       Use corrosion inhibitor into mud system.

                        Ledging can be an issue when drilling alternate hard and soft formations particularly at an angle. This
                      can occur when drilling through the reservoir zones. Ledging occurs generally at the top of the harder
                        formations at the interface when whirl or other lateral instability is induced due to the reduced depth
                         of cut. This can be reduced or eliminated by following negative drill break practices and easing the bit
                          into the harder formation.
  Ledging and hole
       spiraling        Poor weight transfer to the bit can also produce ledging and hole enlargement by reducing the depth
                         of cut at the bit, thus initiating lateral instability and whirl.
                     The higher the bend angle the more likely hole spiraling will occur. To overcome this problem a long
                      gauge bit or turbo-back stabilizer can be used. Another method of reducing hole spiraling is to reduce
                        the distance from bit face to bent housing.
                      Review the offset wells for problems encountered.
                       Hole angles between 45° and 65° present the most problems with drilled cuttings having a tendency
                         to slide down the annulus and ‘pack off’. Hole angles greater than 65° do not present additional
 Poor hole cleaning   problems in this regard since the drilled cuttings are supported by sliding friction against the wellbore
                     and become more stable as discrete cuttings beds. Use good hole cleaning practices to prevent
                        formulation of cutting beds (Rotation, High GPM, Thin Sweeps. . .)
                             Utilizing DV collar.
  Cement quality   QC cement and cement additives.
   and cross flow     Ensure applications and recording of Cement Quality Parameters (CQPs) evaluation.
                        Follow up PEP’s cementing operation procedure.

5. Well Integrity Management Plan
Well Integrity is defined as the application of technical, operational and organizational solutions to
reduce the risk of uncontrolled release of formation fluids to atmosphere or subsurface layers,
throughout the life cycle of a well.
It will be responsibility of Senior Drilling & Completion Supervisor at wellsite and Drilling & Completion
Superintendent in Tehran office to ensure the following certificates are prepared after each job carried
out during the drilling and completion operations of the well and submitted to the respective drilling
engineer for inclusion in the Integrity Management File for the well.
Moreover, a dedicated well integrity input report is generated in WELLVIEW which will pick up data
entered in WELLVIEW during daily drilling and completion reports compilation. The senior drilling and
completion supervisor shall ensure the proper filling of all the reports on daily basis. The following
reports must be filled and sent to drilling engineer at the end of job
    •   Wellbore Sections
    •   Casing Strings (Casing Tally)
    •  Cementing Report
    •  Wellheads Information
    •  Formation Integrity Test Report (If applicable)
Note: For each test performed a well integrity certificate provided in below is to be filled.

10. Drilling Procedures
10.1. Rig Mobilization and Preparations to Spud
•   Survey well location and access road in advance. Review site conditions with Company Witness.
•   Apply moving rig by large modular as much as possible according to the conditions of access road

   and well site, derrick, substructure, mud pump and other equipment shall be wholly moved.
•  Move rig according to designed plan.
•   Install equipment as required by the well site layout. The crown block, rotary table and wellhead

    shall be aligned.
•  The equipment, instrumentation and lighting system provided for the well site shall be explosion

    proof.
•  The total volumes of drilling fluid tanks shall not be less than 2400bbls.
•   Before spud:

   o Ensure all the drill string is inspected as per DS-1 Cat IV.

   o Ensure all lifting gears are inspected appropriately pre-rig move.

   o Prepare all the tools and materials as required, drift, measure and clean drill pipe before first

       pick up.

   o Record GL to RKB height on drilling report.

   o Consult with E&P for wellhead valves orientation.

   o Hold a pre-spud meeting. Ensure all parties are in attendance, all personnel are familiar with

       their roles and responsibilities.

   o Confirm Well control certificates and level for key personnel.

   o  All Well control equipment certified.

10.2. 36" Hole Section
10.2.1. General Information
The 36” interval will be drilled from surface to section TD at 100m, using Bentonite Mud for drilling
and PHG as Hi-Vis Pill to assist in hole cleaning. At section TD the hole will be swept with 50bbl high
viscosity pill followed by 150-200bbl viscous gel mud spotted on the bottom before the 26" casing is
run.

    Casing Point                26” Casing @ 100 m

    Formation                    Aghajari Formation

                                   Rig Subbase Wash out / Erosion, Mud Loss, Almost Problem
    Risks & Hole problems
                                Free

    Deviation Control          TOTCO

    Logging                  N/A

                                                Spud Mud

                       MW (pcf)                     67-68

                                                      Vis. (sec/qt)                   >80

                                     PV (cp)                                     -
     Drilling Fluid Parameters
                                      YP (lb./100ft²)                  >25

                              10 Sec / 10 Min Gel (lb./100ft²)                     -

                                        API FL (ml/ 30min)               NC

                                     PH                         9.5 - 10.5

                               GPM                    300 - 900

     Drilling Parameters              WOB (KLBs)                  10 - 30

                                 RPM                    80 - 100

10.2.2. Sequence of Operation

1.  Check Pre-Spud Check List. Hold Pre – Job Safety Meeting.
2.  Make up 26'' Bit as per BHA design. Tag formation at ±10.5 m.
Note:
    ▪   Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are on well site and are in serviceable condition.
    ▪   Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section of hole are available.
    ▪  Enough Mud Material, LCM and Cement Should be Available before spud the rig to use in case
        of needing.

                             Operations Project

                                  Well Drilling Program - JR-09

    ▪  1 Set cement pump truck should be available on well site before start drilling.
    ▪  Mud Logging unit should be available from rig spud.

3.   Drill ahead formation down to 100 m (26” casing point in Aghajari formation) using hi-vis
    bentonite pill. Pay enough attention to drill straight hole. Control flow rate and take care of wash
    outs below rig sub base.
4. POOH to Surf, P/U 36" HO to enlarge the hole, RIH, Cont. enlarging hole to 100m.

Note:
    ▪  TD should be adjusted to have 2 m of rat hole below casing shoe.
    ▪  The exact TD will be determined based on casing tally.
    ▪  Run Survey to Check inclination @ 50 & 100 m (to ensure the deviation is below 1 degree)

5.  At TD, Circulate and clean the hole. Observe the well. Perform Wiper Trip Prior to running casing.
    Spot viscous mud @ TD. POOH to surface. Check Bit.
6.  Perform Pre-Job Safety meeting (PJSM).
7.  R/Up CSG/ Running Equipment.
8.  Run 26" Casing 136.2# to 100 m with stinger shoe to bottom as per casing program. Casing shoe
    should be adjusted to have 2 m of rat hole and enough stick up (1.5 m on rig floor). Fill casing by
   non-LCM fresh mud.
Note:
    ▪  Do not exert much load and compressing stress on the shoe if encountered tight hole and
        ledges.
    ▪  Make sure that 2 No. of 2” nipple had been welded on conductor and it is plugged w/ a quick
       union low pressure plug.
    ▪   Don’t exceed 80% of collapse rating pressure of casing while pumping (200 psi).
9.   Run stinger on 5" DP’s using the “C” Plate and 5” x 26” centralizer. Sting in. M/U & test
     cementing lines. Circulate for 1.2 or till shaker clean volume. While circulating, check the DPs
      annulus for any return. Use all DPs weight on the string if observing any minor leakage through
     DPs annulus.
10.  Cement casing as per program. Any minor adjustment regarding the corrected depth will be
     done in due time. Displace with mud (1-2 bbl. Short Displace). Monitor the pressures. Record
     and report the final pressure, Sting out. Check the float. POOH one stand, Circulate to
      flush/clean drill pipe. POOH to surface. L/D Stinger While W.O.C to Get Hard, perform top Job If
     Needed.
Note:
    ▪  Based on the results obtained from cementing, decision will be made to perform top-up jobs
       While W.O.C to Get Hard.

11. After cement returns to cellar floor, open the 2" nipple on conductor & flush it.
12. If there is no cement return to surface, a top-up job should be performed to fill the annulus. Use
   same slurry weight as the primary cement slurry. The cement should be accelerated with max.

    (2%) Calcium Chloride BWOC and no other additives. Wait for the top job cement to get hard.
13. Slack Off Weight. Check Cement by slack off weight and check for any movement.
14. Rough Cut 26" Casing, Dress & Bevel Casing Neck. Prepare and Install 29-1/2'' Flange (Locking
    flange). Check Cement by slack off weight. Check for any movement.
15. N/U BOP (29-1/2" Diverter- 500 psi) Bell Nipple & flow line and Related Lines & Valves.
16. Perform diverter function Test.
17. P/U Next BHA and Stand Back 5" DP's as needed.
18. RIH W/ New BHA and 24" Bit #1 (1-1-5) to Tag Shoe, Drill Out Shoe & cement below shoe.

10.3. 24" Hole Section
10.3.1. General Information
This section will be drilled from 100 m at 26” casing shoe to ±1500 m through AGHAJARI, MISHAN and
10 to 30m in GACHSARAN #7 formation as section TD. The section will be drilled with Bentonite mud
receiving from previous section to ±700m then the well will be displaced with KCL / PHPA / Salt
Polymer Mud and continued to section TD. The 18 5/8" casing is run to TD to provide a barrier for
drilling through the Gachsaran formation.

     Casing Point              18 5/8” Casing @ 1500 m

     Formation                    Aghajari, Mishan and Gachsaran Formation

     Risks & Hole problems        Tight Hole, Stuck, Bit Balling, Loss Circulation

     Deviation Control         CDR or Gyro / GR

     Logging                 N/A

                         PHB then Salt/ KCl /PHPA/ Polymer

                       MW (pcf)                   68 - 89

                                                      Vis. (sec/qt)                    38-50

                                     PV (cp)                    ALAP
      Drilling Fluid Parameters
                                      YP (lb./100ft²)                   15-25

                              10 Sec / 10 Min Gel (lb./100ft²)            6-14

                                        API FL (ml/ 30min)                 <5

                                     PH                        9.5 – 10.5

                               GPM                     850-1000

      Drilling Parameters             WOB (KLBs)                    20-45

                                 RPM                      80-120

10.3.2. Sequence of Operation

1.  After D/O of 26'' Casing shoe and Cement Below Shoe, drilling 24" Hole to 103 m with 24" Bit #1
   would be done.
2.  Circulate & Clean the Hole. Adjust bentonite mud weight and circulate to have unified mud in
    hole.
3.  Cont. Drilling 24" Hole till stabilizer below the Casing Shoe, with reduced drilling parameter.

Note:

      POOH, Conduct flow check while POOH and ensure well stable prior to performing wireline
        logging.

    ▪   Drilling fluid will be conditioned per the hole situation after logging. If some more fill was
       detected after logging, then more anti-caving agent will be added into fluid system. If tight

    ▪  Monitor hook loads during running of the casing to detect excessive drag.

    20-3/4" 3K & DSA Locking Tie down Flange. Test the same.

10.3.3. Preventive Measures

    ▪   This section may experience formation cave-in and bit balling, which ultimately may affect
       wellbore stability and cementing quality. Control 3-5% KCl and the concentration will be
       increased as hole dictate to avoid bit balling and cave-in.
    ▪    If observe high Torque fluctuation or vibration at surface, the driller should do drill off test to
       choose proper RPM to relax the BHA vibration.
    ▪  On the bottom of Aghajari and Mishan formation will encounter Red Marl and gradually
       increased till reach to top of Gachsaran, which may lead to bit balling and tight hole, short trip
       per 200m to eliminate the tight hole. Increase MW and control the mud properties as per the
         Drilling Fluid program.
    ▪  Wiper trip to the casing shoe (if hard back reaming, POOH to surface to change Tri-Cone bit),
        RIH, ream any tight spot, then RIH to TD, circulate and condition the mud for RIH casing, Pump
        Hi-Vis at bottom if required.
    ▪   Before connection, back ream and ream down at least one time to check the hole is in good
       shape and then make connection.
    ▪  To prevent overloading the annulus, keep a controlled ROP.
    ▪  Ream any tight spots until the section is clean prior to making connections. Note pick up and
        slack off weight of drill string to identify any abnormal increase in drag and friction.
    ▪  Pump Hi-Vis mud, sweeps per three stands to clean the hole as soon as possible.

10.3.4. 18 5/8" Casing Running/Cementing Preparation

    ▪  18 5/8" Casing Running & Cementing Program will be issued separately.
    ▪  Use API Drift to verify the drift of every joint of casing prior to running. The DS shall physically
       check and confirm the OD of the casing drift. Any joints that cannot be drifted should be clearly
      marked and set aside.
    ▪  Measure the casing at least 2 times to confirm the casing tally's accuracy. Clean and inspection
          all the threads.
    ▪  Double check the float collar, float shoe, confirm the floats in good work condition.
    ▪   Install the casing centralizers as per the final Casing Running & Cementing Program.
    ▪   After Visual Thread Inspection (VTI) is completed and measured for pipe tally, apply API
       modified thread compound and install the protectors hand tight.
    ▪   Ensure all casing running equipment has valid certificates and address the lessons learned
       from the previous casing running in Sepehr-Jufair Oil Field.
    ▪   All BTC casing shall be made up to the base of the triangle.
    ▪   Circulate and wash down the last joint of casing and tag bottom lightly.

      equivalent MW, Resume Drilling Formation to 1505 m with 17" Bit #1.

     Cut and L/D Landing Joint. Dress & bevel casing neck.

10.4.3. Preventive Measures

▪    If observe high Torque fluctuation or vibration at surface, the driller should do drill off test to
   choose proper RPM to relax the BHA vibration.
▪  Wiper trip to the casing shoe (if hard back reaming, POOH to surface to change Tri-Cone bit), RIH,
   ream any tight spot, then RIH to TD, circulate and condition the mud for RIH casing, Pump Hi-Vis
    at bottom if required.
▪  The Gachsaran formation contains Anhydrite which interbedded with gray to red Marl and Salt,
   which may lead to tight spots or tight hole, hard back reaming.
▪  Ream any tight spots until the section is clear prior to making connections. Note P/U and S/O
    weight of string.
▪    It's necessary to flow check prior to POOH, reach the casing shoe and before BHA enter BOPs.
▪  Enough weighting material and kill mud must be stocked on rig site.
▪  BOP drill should be performed on location as policy.
▪   Carefully watch pit level and monito MW of flow line. Control tripping speed to avoid swabbing
   and surging. Condition the mud as per drilling program and hole conditions.

10.4.4. 13 3/8" – 13 5/8" Casing Running/Cementing Preparation

▪  13 3/8" x 13 5/8" Casing Running & Cementing Program will be issued separately.
▪  Use 12.25" Drift to verify the drift of every joint of casing prior to running. The DS shall physically
    check and confirm the OD of the casing drift. Any joints that cannot be drifted should be clearly
   marked and set aside
▪  Measure the casing at least 2 times to confirm the casing tally's accuracy. Clean and inspection all
    the threads.
▪  Double check the float collar, float shoe, confirm the floats in good work condition.
▪   Install the casing centralizers as per the final Casing Running & Cementing Program.
▪   After Visual Thread Inspection (VTI) is completed and measured for pipe tally, apply API modified
    thread compound and install the protectors hand tight.
▪   Ensure all casing running equipment has valid certificates and address the lessons learned from
    the previous casing running in Sepehr-Jufair Oil Field.
▪   Circulate and wash down the last joint of casing and tag bottom lightly.
▪  Check casing tally against the casing shoe depth desired. The casing shoe should be set at 1-2m
    off bottom.
▪   During all the running casing operation, the volume of the flow back and the volume of the casing
    run into the hole shall be observed and record in the trip sheet.
▪   Circulate one bottom to up at least 2 bottoms up or until hole clean. Monitor returns for losses.

10.5. 12 1/4" Hole Section
10.5.1. General Information
This section will be drilled from 2000 m at 13 5/8” casing shoe to ± 2639 m through ASMARI, PABDEH
and GURPI formations as section TD. The section will be drilled with a new build KCL / PHPA / Salt
Polymer CACO3 Mud to section TD. Glycol needs to be ready on location as contingency plan.

     Casing Point              9 5/8’’ Casing @ 2639 m

     Formation                  Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi

                              Swab, Tight Hole, Loss Circulation, Well Flow (Ca++
      Risks & Hole Problems
                                    Increase)

     Deviation control          CDR/ GR – MWD/GR

10.5.2. Sequence of Operation
1.    After D/O of 13 3/8'' Casing shoe and Cement below Shoe, Cont. Drilling 12-1/4" Hole to 2003
   m (W/ 12-1/4” Bit #1 1-3-5). Work bit through the shoe track interval several times with or
      without rotation, pull the bit into shoe.

2.   Work on Junk Sub, Circulate, Clean the Hole. Ensure the unified mud throughout the wellbore,
     Perform FIT w/ 88 pcf equivalent MW. POOH.

3.   P/U New 12-1/4” PDC Bit #2 (Add 12-1/4" S. Stab), RIH to Bottom.

Note:
“The well should be closely monitored during all phases of the cementing operation. The BOPs should
not be nipple down until you are sure that the well will not flow.”

10.5.3. Preventive Measures

▪    If observe high Torque fluctuation or vibration at surface, the driller should do drill off test to
   choose proper RPM to relax the BHA vibration.
▪  Wiper trip to the casing shoe (if hard back reaming, POOH to surface to change Tri-Cone bit), RIH,
   ream any tight spot, then RIH to TD, circulate and condition the mud for RIH casing, Pump Hi-Vis
    at bottom if required.
▪  Ream any tight spots until the section is clear prior to making connections. Note P/U and S/O
    weight of string.
▪    It's necessary to flow check prior to POOH, reach the casing shoe and before BHA enter BOPs.
▪  Wiper trip according to wellbore condition and tight spot indication.
▪   During drilling this hole section tight hole or caving may occur, leading to pack off/pipe stuck.
▪   According to actual condition, if necessary, spot HVP to sweep the hole.
▪  Reduce time for connections stop, check for mud weight, jar should be in good condition, drillers
    should vigilant, ream and back ream to confirm the string is free before making connection.
▪  Make any effort to clean hole for reducing ECD to avoid lost circulation.
▪   Avoid excessive circulation rates and pump surge.
▪  Employ thin mud. Maintaining a low yield point is particularly important to reduce the ECD in the
    annulus. Use mud with minimal gel strength.
▪   Rotate and reciprocate pipe slowly before starting to circulate (breaking circulation). Then break
    circulation by starting pump slowly as drill pipe is raised.
▪  Run in hole slowly to avoid any sudden movement. Do not exceed calculated surge pressure or
    pipe running speed.

10.5.5. 9 5/8" Casing Running/Cementing Preparation

▪  9 5/8" Casing Running & Cementing Program will be issued separately.
▪  Use 8.5" Drift to verify the drift of every joint of casing prior to running. The DS shall physically
    check and confirm the OD of the casing drift. Any joints that cannot be drifted should be clearly
   marked and set aside
▪  Measure the casing at least 2 times to confirm the casing tally's accuracy. Clean and inspection all
    the threads.
▪  Double check the float collar, float shoe, confirm the floats in good work condition.
▪   Install the casing centralizers as per the final Casing Running & Cementing Program.
▪   After Visual Thread Inspection (VTI) is completed and measured for pipe tally, apply API modified
    thread compound and install the protectors hand tight.
▪   Ensure all casing running equipment has valid certificates and address the lessons learned from
    the previous casing running in Sepehr-Jufair Oil Field.
▪   Circulate and wash down the last joint of casing and tag bottom lightly.
▪  Check casing tally against the casing shoe depth desired. The casing shoe should be set at 0.5 - 1m
    off bottom.
▪   During all the running casing operation, the volume of the flow back and the volume of the casing
    run into the hole shall be observed and record in the trip sheet.
▪   Circulate one bottom to up at least 2 bottoms up or until hole clean. Monitor returns for losses.
▪   Chloride and Calcium content in the water to be used for spacer and the slurry should be checked
   ahead of job.
▪   Condition mud property while circulation before performing cement job.
▪  Make sure that the shale shaker is clean of cutting and MW in = MW out.
▪   Rig pump efficiency to be checked accurately by the DS together with the cementing engineer
    before the job and reported in DDR.

10.6.3. Preventive Measure

▪  Wiper trip to the casing shoe (if hard back reaming, POOH to surface to change Tri-Cone bit), RIH,
   ream any tight spot, then RIH to TD, circulate and condition the mud for RIH casing, Pump Hi-Vis
    at bottom if required.
▪  Ream any tight spots until the section is clear prior to making connections. Note P/U and S/O
    weight of string.
▪    It's necessary to flow check prior to POOH, reach the casing shoe and before BHA enter BOPs.
▪  Wiper trip according to wellbore condition and tight spot indication.
▪   During drilling this hole section tight hole or caving may occur, leading to pack off/pipe stuck.
▪   According to actual condition, if necessary, spot HVP to sweep the hole.
▪  Reduce time for connections stop, check for mud weight, jar should be in good condition, drillers
    should vigilant, ream and back ream to confirm the string is free before making connection.
▪  Make any effort to clean hole for reducing ECD to avoid lost circulation.
▪   Avoid excessive circulation rates and pump surge.
▪  Employ thin mud. Maintaining a low yield point is particularly important to reduce the ECD in the
    annulus. Use mud with minimal gel strength.
▪   Rotate and reciprocate pipe slowly before starting to circulate (breaking circulation). Then break
    circulation by starting pump slowly as drill pipe is raised.
▪  Run in hole slowly to avoid any sudden movement. Do not exceed calculated surge pressure or
    pipe running speed.
▪   Drilling fluid will be conditioned per the hole situation after logging. If some more fill was detected
    after logging, then more anti-caving agent  will be added into  fluid system.  If tight hole
    encountered, then the MW should be increased a little more. In addition, the lubricant and
    torque-less should be added into fluid system to reduce friction.

            , L/D Log Tools.

     PDC Bit. RIH to BTM

    ▪   Directional Drilling Program & Final BHA will be issued separately.

14.   Perform condition trip to 3073 m

15.   Circulate out Hi Vis pill to clean hole, perform hole condition in case of OBS tight spot

16.  POOH to SURF. to change bit

10.7.3. Preventive Measure

▪  Ream any tight spots until the section is clear prior to making connections. Note P/U and S/O
    weight of string.
▪    It's necessary to flow check prior to POOH, reach the casing shoe and before BHA enter BOPs.
▪  Wiper trip according to wellbore condition and tight spot indication.
▪   During drilling this hole section tight hole or caving may occur, leading to pack off/pipe stuck.
▪   According to actual condition, if necessary, spot HVP to sweep the hole.
▪  Reduce time for connections stop, check for mud weight, jar should be in good condition, drillers
    should vigilant, ream and back ream to confirm the string is free before making connection.
▪  Make any effort to clean hole for reducing ECD to avoid lost circulation.
▪   Avoid excessive circulation rates and pump surge.
▪  Employ thin mud. Maintaining a low yield point is particularly important to reduce the ECD in the
    annulus. Use mud with minimal gel strength.
▪   Rotate and reciprocate pipe slowly before starting to circulate (breaking circulation). Then break
    circulation by starting pump slowly as drill pipe is raised.
▪  Run in hole slowly to avoid any sudden movement. Do not exceed calculated surge pressure or
    pipe running speed.
▪   Drilling fluid will be conditioned per the hole situation after logging. If some more fill was detected
    after logging, then more anti-caving agent  will be added into  fluid system.  If tight hole
    encountered, then the MW should be increased a little more. In addition, the lubricant and
    torque-less should be added into fluid system to reduce friction.

11.7. 6 1/8" Hole Section (Horizontal Section)
11.7.1. Effective Tension
For drilling 6 1/8" hole section according to below T&D result, the drill string configuration (especially
the length and placement of 3 1/2" DP and 3 1/2" HWDP) must be changed periodically to prevent
drill string buckling while slide drilling and tripping in to reach the planned depth.

"The final configuration of 6 1/8" D.D BHA will be issued with Directional Drilling Program."

                                               Table 37: 36" Hole Section Mud Program

         This section will be drilled to ±100m through AGHAJARI formation, and it contains the red marl and
         clay with a thin bed of sandstone also occasionally trace of Gypsum.

      PHG pill will be used to clean the hole and since Bentonite has the best cake around the wellbore, it
          will make a good cake for hole stability.

       While drilling, the lime will be used to control pH and in order to disperse the formation clay.

             If drilling water has the chloride concentration of more than 1000 mg/Lit, Bentonite will not be
        hydrated well and Xanthan Gum will be used to increase Rheology along with Bentonite.

          Drilling fluid density will be controlled around 67-68pcf. Use available solids control equipment to
        reduce low gravity solids build-up, thus reducing any dilution requirements for density control. Mud
        weight to be adjusted as hole conditions dictate.

        At the beginning of the drilling for the first 20 meters of the drilling, due to prevent the rig subbase
        washout, the mud viscosity must be around 60-70 sec/qt. Then viscosity must be decreased to 40 - 50
         sec/qt. in order to prevent overflow from shakers.

         Yield Point of the Bentonite Mud to be maintained more than 25-40 lb./100ft2 for the first 20m due
        to prevent the rig subbase washout. After drilling 20m, the Yield Point of Bentonite Mud between 18-
       28 lb./100ft2 is enough for sufficient hole cleaning. The Yield Point of PHG between 30-40 lb./100ft2
           is enough for sufficient hole cleaning. Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by
        extensive use of solids control equipment, coupled with whole new mud dilution.

        During normal drilling operations, pH should be kept 10-11. This will maximize chemicals performance
       and minimize corrosion problems. The pH will be adjusted with caustic soda for fresh mud. While

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                 Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production
                             Operations Project

                                  Well Drilling Program - JR-09

 Doc. No:            SJD4   DDRGED   DRDR    PLDR     9001     D01      Page 185 of 281

drilling the pH will be adjusted with the lime (1-2ppb) for controlling of the formation clay dispersion
and prevent mud Rheology build up.

Total hardness should be maintained below 600 mg/L with the addition of Soda Ash and/or Caustic
Soda.

Measuring the MBT is the direct indication of Clay formation reactivity. MBT doesn’t need to be
controlled in this hole section when Bentonite mud designed as this section DF system.

All SCE should be function tested and repaired as necessary prior to spud the well. Dress Shakers with
60 - 80 and mud cleaner with 140 – 175 mesh size screens. Ensure shakers are running immediately
prior to and during all periods of circulation. Use all the solids control equipment available on the rig
site.

Drilling Issues

In case of stuck pipe, 50bbl of un‐weighted PIPE LAX pill at 3.5‐4.5 gal/bbl. of diesel can be pumped
down to the string and every 10min 5bbl spotted around the stuck area while working on the string.

Cleaning cuttings from a vertical hole has been covered extensively by numerous investigators. Hole
cleaning in a vertical hole is essentially a matter of overcoming the slip velocity of the cuttings with
sufficient annular velocity and carrying capacity of the drilling fluid. Although any velocity greater than
the settling velocity of the largest cutting will theoretically lift all the cuttings to surface eventually,
too low an annular velocity will lead to an undesirable high concentration of cuttings in the annulus.
Experience has shown that cuttings concentrations more than 5% by volume cause tight hole or stuck
pipe when circulation is stopped.

The driving parameter that shows the hole cleaning is the 6 and 3 RPM readings. The 6 reading has to
be over 8 all time to ensure good hole cleaning. 30bbl of Hi-Vis Bentonite pill must be pumped every
drilled stand and circulated out of the hole prior to connecting the next stand.

In case of high torque & drag, LUBRICANT or diesel would be used at 1 ‐ 2% by volume.

It is recommended to prevent the bit balling phenomenon by pumping periodically anti-bit balling
pills:

•  LIGNOSULFONATE Brine as Low Vis Pill
    1.   Fill up a pit with required drill water.
    2.  Add NACL and adjust mud weight for 67 to 68pcf as per current mud in the hole.
    3.  Add 5 ppb of LIGNOSULFONATE.
    4.  Add 0.2 ppb of Xanthan Gum to raise the viscosity above 30 – 32 sec/qt.
    5.  Add 5 ppb of Walnut Shell (F) + 5 ppb of Walnut Shell (M).

•   Hi Vis Pill
    1.   Fill up a pit with required volume of current mud in the hole.
    2.  Add 3 ppb of Xanthan Gum to raise the viscosity between 80 to 90 sec/qt.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                 Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production
                             Operations Project

                                  Well Drilling Program - JR-09

 Doc. No:            SJD4   DDRGED   DRDR    PLDR     9001     D01      Page 186 of 281

OR

•  Lime Brine as Low Vis Pill
    1.   Fill up a pit with required drill water.
    2.  Add NACL and adjust mud weight for 67 to 68pcf as per current mud in the hole.
    3.  Add 5 ppb of Lime.
•   Hi Vis Pill
    1.   Fill up a pit with required volume of current mud in the hole.
    2.  Add 3 ppb of Xanthan Gum to raise the viscosity between 80 to 90 sec/qt.

•  Pumping Procedure
    1.  Pumped 50bbl of LIGNOSULFONATE Brine or Lime Brine as low viscous pill.
    2.  Pumped 50bbl of Xanthan Gum Hi Vis Pill.
    3.  Pumped down until LIGNOSULFONATE Brine or Lime Brine come out the bit.
    4.  While keep the bit 1m off bottom, jerking the string, increase the RPM to the maximum
        possible.

As it is seen in geological forecast, soft & sticky marls referred as Gumbo, contained large amount of
SMECTITE and/or ILLITE could be associated with problems such as bit balling, mud rings, plugged flow
lines and hole washout & cause low process of drilling and unnecessary trips and some more
difficulties to drill the section as fast as possible.

The formation fluid influx could affect the mud system without a sign of an increase in the mud volume
which necessitates mud weight increase. The major sign of this influx is the increase in the hardness
and decrease in the pH.

The PHPA will be added to the system after 2 mud cycles, when the mud is warm enough gradually
from 0.25ppb to 1ppb in order to prevent shakers overflow. The concentration must be maintained
while drilling because this chemical goes out of the system by the cuttings.

At this system uses Salt as the source of density, salinity and Clay inhibition in the system. When mud
weight reaches 80pcf the solution must be built as a saturated solution then increase mud weight to
the desired value. While drilling to section TD the mud weight will be increase gradually as per plan or
hole dictation to 89pcf by Barite as weighting agent. Use available solids control equipment to reduce
low gravity solids build-up, thus reducing any dilution requirements for density control. The provision
of keeping on the reserve pits, sufficient quantity of heavy mud as kill mud should be considered. This
will help to prompt increasing mud weight in the shortest time.

Yield Point of the Bentonite Mud to be maintained between 18-28 lb./100ft2 which is enough for
sufficient hole cleaning. While drilling this section with Polymer Mud, XC Polymer will be used as base
of rheology to extend hole cleaning and providing suitable YP and LSRV. Yield Point to be maintained
at a range of 14-20 lb./100ft2. Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by extensive
use of solids control equipment, coupled with new mud dilution.

Due to drilling long sections in Marl and Clay formations, full consideration must be taken on Rheology
to be in the range in order to prevent shooting up Rheology. Increasing in the Rheology will made
further problems such as shaker overflow, increasing in the MW, hole washout, and SPP.

While drilling to 700m with Bentonite Mud the fluid loss will not be controlled. After displacing, the
hole with Salt Polymer Mud the fluid loss will be controlled gradually below 10 cc/30min and gradually
will be decreased to below 5 cc/30min by section TD. Fluid loss will be kept under control by the
addition of polymeric chemicals such as, Starch.

While drilling with Bentonite Mud the pH will be kept at 10-11 in order to have Rheology in the range
and prevent of formation's Clay from flocculating. While drilling with Salt Polymer mud the pH will be
maintained 9.5-10. to achieve the mentioned subject, the pH will be adjusted with caustic soda for
fresh mud and while drilling the pH will be adjusted by Lime (1-2ppb) for controlling the formation's
clay dispersion and prevent mud Rheology build up.

Total hardness should be maintained below 1,200 mg/L with the addition of Soda Ash and/or Caustic
Soda. While drilling this section encounter with Ca2+ based Gypsum is inevitable. Gypsum is calcium
sulfate with water of crystallization (CaSO4.2H2O), Calcium sulfate contamination is similar to cement
contamination because both liberate calcium ions, which in turn cause flocculation. The sulfate ion

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────

                             Operations Project

                                  Well Drilling Program - JR-09

 Doc. No:            SJD4   DDRGED   DRDR    PLDR     9001     D01      Page 191 of 281

contributes to the flocculation of clay solids, although its effect is small compared to calcium ions. The
severity of flocculation depends to a great degree on clay content. When CaSO4 causes the calcium
concentration to increase and viscosity may fluctuate drastically. As calcium ion concentrations
further increase, a base exchange occurs in which sodium montmorillonite becomes calcium
montmorillonite. There are several methods for handling CaSO4 contamination. The drilling fluid can
be maintained as a low-calcium fluid by chemically precipitating by adding soda ash.

Measuring the MBT is the direct indication of Clay formation reactivity. MBT doesn’t need to be
controlled in this hole section when Bentonite mud designed as this section DF system. After displacing
the hole to Salt Polymer mud the MBT must be controlled below 15 ppb by utilizing all solids control
equipment and mud dilution.

All SCE should be function tested and maintained as necessary prior to starts the section. Dress
Shakers with 100-140 mesh size screen and mud cleaner with 170 - 200. Ensure shakers are running
immediately prior to and during all periods of circulation. Use all the solids control equipment
available on the rig site.

Centrifuges must be run immediately after starting drilling as the ROP is high in this section and there
is no sufficient time to discard undesirable solids after the build-up. After adding the Barite to the mud
system, the centrifuges must be run as the Barite recovery system in order to keep Barite in the system
for saving cost and well control purposed.

Drilling Issues

In case of stuck pipe, 50bbl of un‐weighted PIPE LAX pill at 3.5‐4.5 gal/bbl. of diesel can be pumped
down to the string and every 10min 5bbl spotted around the stuck area while working on the string.

Hole cleaning in a vertical hole is essentially a matter of overcoming the slip velocity of the cuttings
with sufficient annular velocity and carrying capacity of the drilling fluid. Although any velocity greater
than the settling velocity of the largest cutting will theoretically  lift all the cuttings to surface
eventually, too low an annular velocity will lead to an undesirable high concentration of cuttings in
the annulus. Experience has shown that cuttings concentrations more than 5% by volume cause tight
hole or stuck pipe when circulation is stopped.

The driving parameter that shows the hole cleaning is the 6 and 3 RPM readings. The 6 reading has to
be over 6 all time to ensure good hole cleaning. 30bbl of Hi-Vis Bentonite pill must be pumped every
drilled stand and circulated out of the hole prior to connecting the next stand while drilling with the
Bentonite Mud and 30bbl of Hi-Vis of Salt Polymer Mud build with Xanthan Gum while drilling with
the Salt Polymer Mud.

Prior to tripping, if any concern exists in regard to hole cleanliness, consideration should be given to
pumping a high weight pill while on bottom. This is especially important if no pills have been pumped
during the section drilled. Returns of all such pills at the shakers should be monitored to gauge their
effectiveness. Care should be exercised to ensure that excessive amounts of high-density pills are not

pumped due to their effect on hydrostatic head. In the case of all pills do not stop or reduce the
circulation rate before the pill(s) have been evacuated from hole. To do so will result in material
dropping out of the pill. Circulation should continue if solids are still coming over the shakers.

Before POOH for casing running follow below procedure:
•   Prepare 300 bbl. (it is not included dead volume) FL controlled pill (FL<3)
•    Pill weight should 2pcf upper from system weight
•   Spot 300 bbl. of this pill at bottom

In case of high torque & drag, LUBRICANT or diesel would be used at 1 ‐ 2% by volume.

It is recommended to prevent the bit balling phenomenon by pumping periodically anti-bit balling
pills:

•  LIGNOSULFONATE Brine as Low Vis Pill
    1.   Fill up a pit with required drill water.
    2.  Add NACL and adjust mud weight for 67 to 68pcf as per current mud in the hole.
    3.  Add 5 ppb of LIGNOSULFONATE.
    4.  Add 0.2 ppb of Xanthan Gum to raise the viscosity above 30 – 32 sec/qt.
    5.  Add 5 ppb of Walnut Shell (F) + 5 ppb of Walnut Shell (M).
•   Hi Vis Pill
    1.   Fill up a pit with required volume of current mud in the hole.
    2.  Add 3 ppb of Xanthan Gum to raise the viscosity between 80 to 90 sec/qt.

OR

•  Lime Brine as Low Vis Pill
    1.   Fill up a pit with required drill water.
    2.  Add NACL and adjust mud weight for 67 to 68pcf as per current mud in the hole.
    3.  Add 5 ppb of Lime.
•   Hi Vis Pill
    1.   Fill up a pit with required volume of current mud in the hole.
    2.  Add 3 ppb of Xanthan Gum to raise the viscosity between 80 to 90 sec/qt.
•  Pumping Procedure
    1.  Pumped 50bbl of LIGNOSULFONATE Brine or Lime Brine as low viscous pill.
    2.  Pumped 50bbl of Xanthan Gum Hi Vis Pill.
    3.  Pumped down until LIGNOSULFONATE Brine or Lime Brine come out the bit.
    4.  While keep the bit 1m off bottom, jerking the string, increase the RPM to the maximum
        possible.

        After drilling the cement inside the casing and before drill out the shoe track with carried mud from
       previous section the old Salt Polymer Mud will be displaced with new 120pcf fresh Salt Saturated Mud
       to drilling this hole section.

       Saturated Salt Muds are primarily used to prevent excessive hole enlargement while drilling massive
         salt beds. They can also be used to reduce the dispersion and hydration of shales and clays.

      The chloride content of saturated salt muds is 188,000 mg/l at saturation. As the temperature of the
     mud increases, more salt is able to go into the solution. This means that a fluid which is saturated
       under surface conditions may not be saturated in downhole temperatures and can cause substantial
      washout in a salt zone due to increased salt solubility.

       At this system uses Salt as the source of density, salinity and Clay inhibition in the system. Salt
       saturated solution must be used to build the mud for this section. While drilling to section TD the mud
       weight will be increase gradually as per plan or hole dictation from 120pcf to 137pcf by Barite and Fer-
       O-Bar as a weighting agent. The Fer-O-Bar will be used from 125pcf to desired mud weight with a ratio
        of 3:1 Barite / Fer-O-Bar. Use available solids control equipment to reduce low gravity solids build-up,
       thus reducing any dilution requirements for density control. The provision of keeping on the reserve
         pits, a sufficient quantity of heavy mud as kill mud should be considered. This will help to prompt
        increasing mud weight in the shortest time.

       While mixing heavy mud of this section, the XC Polymer will not be used at all or used only 0.2 ppb as
       the base of rheology to provide the suitable YP and LSRV for suspending weighting agent materials.
        Yield Point to be maintained at a range of 16-30 lb./100ft2 while drilling with Salt Saturated Mud to
       have sufficient hole cleaning. Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by extensive
       use of solids control equipment, coupled with new mud dilution.

Due to drilling Marl and Clay formations, full consideration must be taken on Rheology to be in the
range in order to prevent shooting up Rheology. Increasing the Rheology will made further problems
such as shaker overflow, increase in the MW, hole washout, and SPP.

While drilling the hole with Salt Saturated Mud the fluid loss will be controlled below 3 cc/30min to
section TD. Fluid loss will be kept under control by the addition of Starch LV.

While drilling pH will be kept at 9-10 in order to have Rheology in the range and prevent of formation's
Clay from flocculating. To achieve the mentioned subject, the pH will be adjusted with caustic soda
for fresh mud and while drilling the pH will be adjusted by Lime (1-2ppb) for controlling the formation's
clay dispersion and prevent mud Rheology build up.

Foaming  is generally restricted to surface foam and  is not troublesome unless aggravated by
mechanical agitation. The degree of foaming may sometimes be decreased by increasing the alkalinity
of the mud (Pm). A De-foaming agent may be necessary. Unless Mg++ sensitive additives are used, a
Saturated Salt Mud is less prone to foam and air cut with a 9.5-10 pH.

Control of the pH of saturated salt muds varies widely. Saturated salt muds require larger additions of
caustic soda to maintain a pH in Salt Saturate Muds. Maintaining an ± 9.5 pH offers several advantages:

•  De flocculants are more effective
•   Corrosion is reduced
•  Lower concentrations of filtration control additives are required when Ca++ and Mg++ solubility
     is reduced
•  Foaming tendency is lessened
•  Mud is generally more stable

Total hardness should be maintained below 1,300 mg/L with the addition of Soda Ash and/or Caustic
Soda. while drilling this section encounter with Ca2+ based Anhydrite is inevitable. There are several
methods for handling CaSO4 contamination. The drilling fluid can be maintained as a low-calcium fluid
by chemically precipitating by adding soda ash.

Saturated salt muds will normally contain soluble calcium due to the formations penetrated and the
type of makeup water used. In addition, the sodium ions from the salt will undergo a base exchange
and release calcium ions from the clay platelets, thereby contributing to the free calcium. Generally,
the presence of calcium does not produce detrimental effects on the mud; except when the pH is
increased beyond 12.0 and then the fluid loss will be difficult to control.

Ca++ and Mg++ hardness less than 1500 mg/lt do not adversely affect filtration control in Saturated
Salt Muds when using starch, however, the hardness of the system will be maintained below 1300
mg/lt by using Soda Ash, Caustic, and dilution.

The MBT must be controlled below 7.5 ppb by utilizing all solids control equipment and mud dilution
in order to have stability in the mud.

       13.5. 12 1/4" Hole Section Mud Program

Drilling Fluid System         KCL / PHPA / Salt Polymer CACO3 Mud (Glycol Contingency)

                             Fresh Water, Soda Ash, Caustic Soda, Lime, Salt, Starch LV, PAC LV, KCL, XC. Polymer, PHPA
Key Products
                               (Glycol Contingency)

Water Type                    Drill/Fresh Water + Waste Water

Solid Control                 Shale Shaker, DESANDER, DESILTER, VFD Centrifuge

Potential Problems          Swab, Tight Hole, Loss Circulation, Well Flow (Ca++ Increase)

                                             Interval Mud Properties

             Funnel      Plastic                                                Chloride      Total
                                       Yield point   Gel Strength  API Fluid Loss
MW (PCF)    Viscosity    viscosity                                                 (mg/Lit)    Hardness    KCL    pH

               (sec/qt.)      (Cp.)                                           * 1,000     (mg/Lit)

 73–88     40–50     ALAP     14–20     3–6 / 4–8       < 3      125–195    < 800    5–7   9–9.5

                                             Table 52: 12 1/4" Hole Section Mud Program

      The fluid for this section is one designed to give proper inhibition to the formations to be able to drill
       through the troublesome argillaceous limestone, shale and marls. This inhibition will be achieved with
      KCL at range of 5-7%wt, PHPA at range of 0.25-1ppb and Glycol at range of 1-3 %vol. (Contingency).

      The PHPA will be added to the system after 2 mud cycles, when the mud is warm enough gradually
      from 0.25ppb to 1ppb in order to prevent shakers overflow. The concentration must be maintained
       while drilling because this chemical goes out of the system by the cuttings. The Glycol as contingency
       chemical will be added to the system, when the mud is homogenized. The started concentration is 1
       percent by volume. Then after checking the mud properties and ensuring that the mud is stable, the
       concentration can increase to 3 percent by volume stepwise.

      The clay and marl inhibitors in the system are potassium ion for cation exchange with the clays, to
       reduce hydration and swelling, and PHPA partially hydrolysed polyacrylamide to encapsulate drilled
        cutting for more effective solids removal efficiency on surface and avoid the clay and marl cuttings to
      be dispersed in mud system prior to be passed over the shakers.

        In Addition, Glycol behaviour causes the polyglycol to become insoluble or precipitate out of solution
        at a certain temperature and salinity. Thus, resulting in glycol-coated clays that are somewhat water-
        repellent.

      The chloride content of KCL / PHPA / Salt Polymer Mud is 125,000 - 195,000 mg/l at saturation. As the
       temperature of the mud increases, more salt is able to go into the solution. This means that a fluid
       which is saturated under surface conditions may not be saturated in downhole temperatures and can
       cause substantial washout in a salt zone due to increased salt solubility.

       At this system uses KCL / NACL salts as the source of density, salinity and clay inhibition in the system.
        Salt saturated solution must be used to build the mud when the mud weight reach to 78pcf for this
        section. For preparing the 73pcf KCL / PHPA / Salt Polymer Mud, the salt solution weight with 20ppb

                             Operations Project

                                  Well Drilling Program - JR-09

 Doc. No:            SJD4   DDRGED   DRDR    PLDR     9001     D01      Page 203 of 281

KCL and addition of NACL must be 70pcf then adding the rest of the chemicals to get 73pcf mud weight.
While drilling to section TD the mud weight will be increase gradually as per plan or hole dictation
from 73pcf to 88pcf by calcium carbonate as a weighting and bridge agent. Controlling of MW could
be done by running SCE (Centrifuges) and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens & dumping
the sand trap and dilution. The provision of keeping on the reserve pits, a sufficient quantity of heavy
mud as kill mud should be considered. This will help to prompt increasing mud weight in the shortest
time.

Maintain the Yield point around 14 to 20 lb/100ft² to ensure adequate hole cleaning, making
adjustment with fresh mud or water as required. XC. Polymer will be used to provide an optimized
rheological profile with elevated low-shear-rate-viscosity and high shear-thinning characteristics,
which result in fluid with inverted flow properties with yield point greater than plastic viscosity.

Care must be taken of shakers overflow while adding PHPA to the system because it will make an
appearance Rheology.

Circulate viscous pill sweeps as required for additional hole cleaning. When TD is reached, a minimum
of two circulations should be pumped prior to make a wiper trip to surface, followed by a circulation
when back on bottom prior to pull out to run 9 5/8" casing.

While drilling the hole with KCL / PHPA / Salt Polymer Mud the API fluid loss will be controlled below
3 cc/30min to section TD. Fluid loss will be kept under control by the addition of Starch LV and PAC
LV. The addition of calcium carbonate as a weighting agent will improve filter cake and help lower API
Fluid loss. It is strictly forbidden to add Starch and PAC LV directly into the active system. All the
treatments must be done as a pre-mix.

The pH should be maintained around 9. to 9.5 using Caustic Soda and Soda Ash. This will maximize
chemicals performance and minimize corrosion problems. pH above 10 will cause to convert PHPA to
be full hydrolysed and loss its effect of encapsulation. pH should not be increased to be above 10.

Total hardness of water should be maintained below 400 mg/L prior to start mixing the other
chemicals for optimum polymer performance with the addition of Soda Ash. Total hardness should be
maintained below 800 mg/L with the addition of Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda while drilling this
section. All The premix that uses to add to the system as dump and dilution must be treated for total
hardness below 400 mg/lt.

Measuring of the MBT is the direct indication of formation reactivity. MBT below 7.5 lb/bbl. is
acceptable. Above this range, API fluid loss will start to shoot up to uncontrollable levels. Using fine
screens & high-speed centrifuges will help in maintaining lower values of MBT by discarding the fine
solids and consequently minimize the dilution rate.

Shakers to be dressed initially with 100/120 mesh screens and after two or three cycles when the mud
polymers are sheared enough dress with finer mesh sizes. Meanwhile drilling could be started with
low concentration of PHPA (0.2-0.3 lb/bbl. is recommended) after mud became heated and fully
sheared increase PHPA concentration to desired range. It has been experienced that the screen sizes
with 175 - 200 API sizes can be applied while drilling this section. There may be a requirement to dress

                             Operations Project

                                  Well Drilling Program - JR-09

 Doc. No:            SJD4   DDRGED   DRDR    PLDR     9001     D01      Page 204 of 281

the shakers with coarser screens for a number of circulations in order to minimize loss of mud on
shakers. Ensure shakers are running immediately prior to and during all periods of circulation.

Use all the solids control equipment available on the rig site. The combination of linear motion shale
shaker with centrifuge proved best results. Centrifuge should be run at all the time if available at high
flow rate on LGS mode (High Speed) to remove low gravity solids and keep mud weight & properties
in range. Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment. All
efforts should be made to maintain the LGS below 6%.

Drilling Issues

Experience has shown that cuttings concentrations more than 5% by volume cause tight hole or stuck
pipe when circulation is stopped. The driving parameter that shows the hole cleaning is the 6 and 3
RPM readings. The 6 reading has to be over 5 all time to ensure good hole cleaning. 30bbl of Hi-Vis pill
must be pumped every drilled stand and circulated out of the hole prior to connecting the next stand
while drilling.

Prior to tripping,  if any concern exists about hole cleanliness, consideration should be given to
pumping a high weight pill while on bottom. This is especially important if no pills have been pumped
during the section drilled. Returns of all such pills at the shakers should be monitored to gauge their
effectiveness. Care should be exercised to ensure that excessive amounts of high-density pills are not
pumped due to their effect on hydrostatic head. In the case of all pills do not stop or reduce the
circulation rate before the pill(s) have been evacuated from hole. To do so will result in material
dropping out of the pill. Circulation should continue if solids are still coming over the shakers.

Before POOH for casing running follow below procedure:
•   Prepare 300 bbl. (it is not included dead volume) FL controlled pill (FL<3), KCL: 7 %wt.
•    Pill weight should 2pcf upper from system weight
•   Spot 300 bbl. of this pill at bottom

After KOP the well is deviated and the hole cleaning concern is for cleaning the deviated section. It is
noticeable, that cutting beds are created in the deviated part of the hole, and pumping tandem pills
(15bbl Low viscous pill followed by 30bbl weighted viscous pill) is strictly required to remove curing
beds.

In case of high torque & drag, LUBRICANT or diesel would be used at 1 ‐ 2% by volume.

shaker with centrifuge proved best results. Centrifuge should be run at all the time if available at high
flow rate on LGS mode (High Speed) to remove low gravity solids and keep mud weight & properties
in range. Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment. All
efforts should be made to maintain the LGS below 6%.

Drilling Issues

In case of stuck pipe, 50bbl of un‐weighted PIPE LAX pill at 3.5‐4.5 gal/bbl. of diesel can be pumped
down to the string and every 10min 5bbl spotted around the stuck area while working on the string.

The driving parameter that shows the hole cleaning is the 6 and 3 RPM readings. The 6 reading has to
be over 5 all time to ensure good hole cleaning. 30bbl of Hi-Vis pill must be pumped every drilled stand
and circulated out of the hole prior to connecting the next stand while drilling.

Prior to tripping,  if any concern exists about hole cleanliness, consideration should be given to
pumping a high weight pill while on bottom. This is especially important if no pills have been pumped
during the section drilled. Returns of all such pills at the shakers should be monitored to gauge their
effectiveness. Care should be exercised to ensure that excessive amounts of high-density pills are not
pumped due to their effect on hydrostatic head. In the case of all pills do not stop or reduce the
circulation rate before the pill(s) have been evacuated from hole. To do so will result in material
dropping out of the pill. Circulation should continue if solids are still coming over the shakers.

Before POOH for casing running follow below procedure:
•   Prepare 300 bbl. (it is not included dead volume) FL controlled pill (FL<3), KCL: 7 %wt.
•    Pill weight should 2pcf upper from system weight
•   Spot 300 bbl. of this pill at bottom

This section is deviated and the hole cleaning concern is for cleaning the deviated section. It is
noticeable, that cutting beds are created in the deviated part of the hole, and pumping tandem pills
(15bbl Low viscous pill followed by 30bbl weighted viscous pill) is strictly required to remove curing
beds.

Circulate and sweep the hole with tandem pill of low viscous and weighted viscous pill periodically
after each drilled stand for hole cleaning because this section is deviated to horizontally.

In case of high torque & drag, LUBRICANT or diesel would be used at 1 ‐ 2% by volume.

       13.7. 6 1/8" Hole Section Mud Program
