                                             Table 62: 6 1/8" Hole Section Mud Program

      The fluid for this section is one designed to give proper inhibition to the formations to be able to drill
       through the troublesome argillaceous limestone, shale and marls. This inhibition will be achieved with
      KCL at range of 5-7%wt, PHPA at range of 0.25-1ppb and Glycol at range of 1-3 %vol. (Contingency).

      The Glycol as contingency chemical will be added to the system, when the mud is homogenized. The
        started concentration is 1 percent by volume. Then after checking the mud properties and ensuring
        that the mud is stable, the concentration can increase to 3 percent by volume stepwise.

      The chloride content of KCL / Salt Polymer Mud is 150,000 - 195,000 mg/l at saturation. As the
       temperature of the mud increases, more salt is able to go into the solution. This means that a fluid
       which is saturated under surface conditions may not be saturated in downhole temperatures and can
       cause substantial washout in a salt zone due to increased salt solubility.

       At this system uses KCL / NACL salts as the source of density, salinity and clay inhibition in the system.
        Salt saturated solution must be used to build the mud for this section. For preparing the 85pcf KCL /
      PHPA / Salt Polymer Mud, the salt solution weight with 22ppb KCL and addition of NACL must be 75pcf
       then adding the rest of the chemicals to get 85pcf mud weight. While drilling to section TD the mud
       weight will be increase gradually as per plan or hole dictation from 85pcf to 87pcf by calcium
       carbonate as a weighting and bridge agent. Controlling of MW could be done by running SCE
        (Centrifuges) and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens & dumping the sand trap and dilution.
      The provision of keeping on the reserve pits, a sufficient quantity of heavy mud as kill mud should be
       considered. This will help to prompt increasing mud weight in the shortest time.

       Maintain the Yield point around 14 to 20 lb/100ft² to ensure adequate hole cleaning, making
       adjustment with fresh mud or water as required. XC. Polymer will be used to provide an optimized

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                 Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production
                             Operations Project

                                  Well Drilling Program - JR-09

 Doc. No:            SJD4   DDRGED   DRDR    PLDR     9001     D01      Page 215 of 281

rheological profile with elevated low-shear-rate-viscosity and high shear-thinning characteristics,
which result in fluid with inverted flow properties with yield point greater than plastic viscosity.

While drilling the hole with KCL / Salt Polymer Mud the API fluid loss will be controlled below 3
cc/30min to section TD. Fluid loss will be kept under control by the addition of Starch LV and PAC LV.
The addition of calcium carbonate as a weighting agent will improve filter cake and help lower API
Fluid loss. It is strictly forbidden to add Starch and PAC LV directly into the active system. All the
treatments must be done as a pre-mix.

The pH should be maintained around 9 to 10 using Caustic Soda and Soda Ash. This will maximize
chemicals performance and minimize corrosion problems.

Total hardness of water should be maintained below 400 mg/L prior to start mixing the other
chemicals for optimum polymer performance with the addition of Soda Ash. Total hardness should be
maintained below 800 mg/L with the addition of Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda while drilling this
section. All The premix that uses to add to the system as dump and dilution must be treated for total
hardness below 400 mg/lt.

Measuring of the MBT is the direct indication of formation reactivity. MBT below 7.5 lb/bbl. is
acceptable. Above this range, API fluid loss will start to shoot up to uncontrollable levels. Using fine
screens & high-speed centrifuges will help in maintaining lower values of MBT by discarding the fine
solids and consequently minimize the dilution rate.

Shakers to be dressed initially with 100/120 mesh screens and after two or three cycles when the mud
polymers are sheared enough dress with finer mesh sizes. It has been experienced that the screen
sizes with 175 - 200 API sizes can be applied while drilling this section. There may be a requirement to
dress the shakers with coarser screens for a number of circulations in order to minimize loss of mud
on shakers. Ensure shakers are running immediately prior to and during all periods of circulation.

Use all the solids control equipment available on the rig site. The combination of linear motion shale
shaker with centrifuge proved best results. Centrifuge should be run at all the time if available at high
flow rate on LGS mode (High Speed) to remove low gravity solids and keep mud weight & properties
in range. Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment. All
efforts should be made to maintain the LGS below 6%.

hardness below 400 mg/lt.

Measuring of the MBT is the direct indication of formation reactivity. MBT below 7.5 lb/bbl. is
acceptable. Above this range, API fluid loss will start to shoot up to uncontrollable levels. Using fine
screens & high-speed centrifuges will help in maintaining lower values of MBT by discarding the fine
solids and consequently minimize the dilution rate.

Shakers to be dressed initially with 100/120 mesh screens and after two or three cycles when the mud
polymers are sheared enough dress with finer mesh sizes. It has been experienced that the screen
sizes with 175 - 200 API sizes can be applied while drilling this section. There may be a requirement to
dress the shakers with coarser screens for a number of circulations in order to minimize loss of mud
on shakers. Ensure shakers are running immediately prior to and during all periods of circulation.

Use all the solids control equipment available on the rig site. The combination of linear motion shale
shaker with centrifuge proved best results. Centrifuge should be run at all the time if available at high
flow rate on LGS mode (High Speed) to remove low gravity solids and keep mud weight & properties
in range. Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment. All
efforts should be made to maintain the LGS below 6%.

Drilling Issues

In case of stuck pipe, 50bbl of un‐weighted PIPE LAX pill at 3.5‐4.5 gal/bbl. of diesel can be pumped
down to the string and every 10min 5bbl spotted around the stuck area while working on the string.

Prior to tripping,  if any concern exists about hole cleanliness, consideration should be given to
pumping a high weight pill while on bottom. This is especially important if no pills have been pumped
during the section drilled. Returns of all such pills at the shakers should be monitored to gauge their
effectiveness. Care should be exercised to ensure that excessive amounts of high-density pills are not
pumped due to their effect on hydrostatic head. In the case of all pills do not stop or reduce the
circulation rate before the pill(s) have been evacuated from hole. To do so will result in material
dropping out of the pill. Circulation should continue if solids are still coming over the shakers.

Before POOH for casing running follow below procedure:

•   Prepare 300 bbl. (it is not included dead volume) FL controlled pill (FL<3), KCL: 7 %wt.
•    Pill weight should 2pcf upper from system weight
•   Spot 300 bbl. of this pill at bottom

This section is deviated and the hole cleaning concern is for cleaning the deviated section. It is
noticeable, that cutting beds are created in the deviated part of the hole, and pumping tandem pills
(15bbl Low viscous pill followed by 30bbl weighted viscous pill) is strictly required to remove curing
beds.

Circulate and sweep the hole with tandem pill of low viscous and weighted viscous pill periodically
after each drilled stand for hole cleaning because this section is deviated to horizontally.

In case of high torque & drag, LUBRICANT or diesel would be used at 1 ‐ 2% by volume.

      The required volume of 85pcf CACL2 brine will prepare and filtrated to be solid free then displace in

                                               Table 72: Completion Fluid Program

        All cleaning should be done well in advance wherever possible. To clean pits and lines, 100bbl of water
       containing 1 to 2 drums of Chemical Wash (Detergent Pill) should be mixed up and circulated through
         all lines, gun lines, mixing lines, etc. This can also be used to clean the tank system initially.

            1.  Flash & clean surface pits (All required pits).
            2.  Clean the mixing hoppers and related lines.
            3.  Clean the ditches line from shakers to suction pit after displacement is over.
            4.  Clean shakers while bypass sand traps after displacement.
            5.  Clean the trip tank after displacement.

     Completion Fluid Mixing Procedure

            1.   Fill up clean reserve pits with required fresh water.
            2.  Added 183 ppb CACL2 to weight up at 85 PCF.
            3.  Added 0.5-1 ppb lime to adjust PH about 9-10.
            4.  Filtered 85 PCF completion fluid from reserve pits to suction pit.
            5.  Check NTU < 50 and recode NTU.
            6.  Check TSS < 50 and recode TSS.
            7.  Added 1 %v/v Corrosion Inhibitor in suction pit. (From top of pit)
            8.  Added 0.5 %v/v H2S Scavenger in suction pit. (From top of pit)
            9.  Added 0.5 %v/v Oxygen Scavenger in suction pit. (From top of pit)
          10. Added 0.5 % v/v Biocide (Anti-Bacterial) in suction pit. (From top of pit)

   Displacement Procedure

         1.  HPJSM and review pit management plan with all involved crew.
         2.  Circulate and condition mud.
         3. Pump 60bbl of 85 PCF Hi-Vis brine pill as spacer.
         4.  Start to pumping 85 PCF filtered brine from suction pit to the hole while return mud to
            dedicated pits as per pit management plan.
         5. When 85 PCF filtered brine on shaker then stop circulation.
         6.  Clean the ditches line from shakers to suction pit.
         7.  Bypass sand traps and clean shakers.
         8.  Take return brine to suction pit.

16. Specific Recommendations for Drilling Optimization

1.  Minimize time in the slips and keep pipe moving at all other times when not in the slips.
    Reciprocation is preferable to rotation in this aspect; the reciprocation distance shall be more than
   5m.

2.  Applying Reciprocation with the Rotating Off-Bottom operation ensures that the wear resulting
   from the tool joint and inner casing wall contact is distributed over the entire stroke length of
    reciprocation, thereby reducing the effect of wear at any particular contact point.
   However, if the drill string is not reciprocated with Rotating Off-Bottom, the wear resulting from
    tool joint contact with casing wall is concentrated at just one contact point only. As a result, for
    the same amount of operation time, Rotating Off-Bottom without any reciprocation will result in
    significantly higher wear on the casing as compared to a case when reciprocation is applied.

3.  Perform a wiper trip every 200~400m according to the actual condition.
4.  Place a ditch magnet at outlet to collect metal filings, report the weight in daily drilling report.
5.  During drilling, it is necessary to drill smoothly, strictly avoid drilling string inappropriately braked
   and percussion drilling and pay attention to the variation of rotary table torque. Prevent bit
    accidents.
6.  While drilling in Chert formation, sticky and slip formation, the surface torque may be abnormal
    higher and drastic fluctuated, the driller should adjust the WOB and RPM, find out proper WOB
   and RPM to reduce the torque fluctuation. Normally if 10% Cherts, control the WOB<15 klb., RPM
   80~100, if 20% Chert, insert cone bit will be considered. The driller should understand long time
    torque fluctuation with same WOB will lead to BHA fatigue damage soon.
7.  Accurately judge the utilization state of bit and grasp the time of replacing the bit well. While
     drilling in argillaceous limestone formation, shale formation, or claystone formation, the ROP may
   be very low 0.5~1.5m, the torque may very low also, the surface parameters are similar like bit
    dull or bit balling, more patients should be paid on this, POOH only after fully considered and
   compared with offset wells drilling performance.
8.   If SPP decrease sharply and hook load decrease at same time, circulate one bottoms up POOH to
    check the BHA; If SPP decrease slowly and no change on hook load, then:
        a.  Check the surface equipment first, the surface circulate system, mud pumps one by one.

       b.  After confirmation of all the surface equipment are in work condition, POOH to check

          the BHA, do not circulate long time.

        c.  The tool pusher check every stand on the pipe body and connections, if no wash out

        was found, inspect all the BHA before RIH, or RIH joint by joint to check every joint

          thoroughly until find the root cause of the SPP dropping.

9. When replacing the bit, measure the outer diameter of the bit, in case of serious wear, RIH and
   reaming down slowly must be performed to prevent bit stuck.
10. Stabilize the drill string to minimize wall contact. Consider the use of under-gauge stabilizers
    further up the string.
11. Utilize Hi-Vis sweep at section TD and prior to wiper trips, only if needed. Use with caution, since

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                 Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production
                             Operations Project

                                  Well Drilling Program - JR-09

 Doc. No:            SJD4   DDRGED   DRDR    PLDR     9001     D01      Page 256 of 281

    the overuse of such pills can quickly affect the viscosity of the active mud system. Once the pills
   have been pumped, do not stop the pumps until they have returned at the shakers. Hi Vis sweeps
    should be caught and segregated or if not able to do so efficiently, that sweep must be dumped
    to reduce the chance of increasing Vis of active mud.
12. According to the hole condition, ream down and clean out that section several times and make
    sure no debris and no drag are observed.
13. Hole Cleaning Guidelines:
    Best drilling practices shall be adopted in order to void annulus overloading / cutting settling
   around BHA during connections / bridges around the DP.
   The following guideline shall be followed:
    •  Ream each stand prior to connection
    •  Sweep hole with Hi-Vis pills periodically
    •  Monitor the mud carrying capacity after any change in the rheology
    •  Minimize the ECD by keeping low YPs
14. Tripping out guidelines
   The following guideline apply for tripping out
    •  Record periodically P/U, S/O weight, on bottom & off bottom Torque and chart the related
        trends.
    •  POOH without pumping & Rotating (on the elevator) and monitor the P/U weight trend by
       comparing the results recorded while drilling.

17.5. Pressure Test Requirements
•   All pressure tests shall be performed according to API RP53.
•   Rig crew must be alerted when pressure test operations are underway. No one must
   remain in the test area.
•   All tests must be performed using clear water.
•  Should any of the tests identify faulty equipment, drilling operations must be suspended
   and well secured, if needed, until the faulty equipment is repaired or replaced.
•   All valves located downstream of the valve being tested must be placed in the OPEN
    position.
•   All pressure tests must be held for a minimum duration of 5 minutes with no observable
   pressure decline. (Low pressure test w/250-300 psi for 5 minutes and high pressure test
   w/max 70% of WP for 10 minutes)
•  Pressure should be released only through pressure release lines.
•  Only authorized personnel go in the test area to inspect for leaks when the equipment is
   under pressure.
•   All lines and connections that are used in the test procedure should be adequately
   secured.
•  Tightening or repair work must be done only after pressure has been released and all
    parties have ensured that there is no possibility of trapped pressure.
•   All pressure tests must be conducted with a test pump. Avoid the use of rig pumps for
   pressure testing. Cement units are acceptable.
•   All test result must be documented in addition to the pressure chart.
•  Top drive IBOP's should be inflow tested up to rated working pressure as initial.
•  With all BOP equipment installed on the wellhead, any pressure test to be performed shall
   not exceed 80% of the internal pressure strengthen on the casing in the well.
•  Each part in choke lines be tested respectively to its rated working pressure.
•  The relief lines be pressure tested to no less than 1450 psi.

17.6. Pressure Testing of Well Control Equipment
•  BOP equipment must be pressure tested as per the following criteria:
   o When installed.
   o  Before drilling out each string of casing.
   o  Following the disconnection or  repair  of any wellbore pressure  seal  in the
      wellhead/BOP stack (limited to the affected components only).
   o  After a maximum of 14 days from last pressure test.
•   All BOP pressure tests must be witnessed by DSV and Rig Manager.
•  A pressure test is required after the installation of casing rams. This test is limited to the

   components affected by the disconnection of the pressure containment seal.
•   All well control equipment except annular BOP’s is to be tested to the lowest of the
    following criteria after the installation of any wellhead body component or prior to drilling
   out cement inside each casing string.
   o  Maximum anticipated wellhead pressure to be encountered in the hole section being
        drilled.
   o  70% of casing burst pressure.
   o  Wellhead rated pressure.
   o  BOP rated pressure.
•  Annular preventer will be tested to a minimum of 70% of the rated working pressure.
•  Annular preventer should be tested with the smallest OD pipe to be used.
•   All high pressure connections associated with the well control equipment are to be
   pressure tested upon the installation or reinstallation of each connection.
•  The volume of test fluid must be monitored and recorded. The opening and closing
   volumes of all BOP functions must be monitored and recorded.
•   All casing pack-offs are to be pressure tested.
•  When testing wellhead components due consideration must be given to burst and
    collapse rating of relevant casing and components.
•  Well control equipment that has been subject to any modification or body repair is to be
   pressure tested and, if applicable, re-certified before use.
•  Wellheads and drilling spools must have full bore double valve isolation whilst the
   wellhead is in communication with open formation. The non-active spool side outlet
   should have a Valve Removable Plug (VRP) installed to enable the installation of valves if
    necessary.

17.7. Casing Integrity Test
•   All surface, intermediate and production casing/liners shall be pressure tested prior to
    drilling out the shoe track or perforating.
•  For surface and intermediate casings/liners the minimum pressure test must be the
    highest of:
   o  Calculated surface pressure required to perform the planned leak off test plus a test
       margin. The recommended test margin for development wells is 4 pcf.
   o  Calculated pressure for circulating out maximum kick as used in casing design
        calculations.
•  For production casing/liners, the minimum pressure test must be equivalent to the shut
    in tubing pressure on top of the annulus completion fluid.
•  Any additional loads that are to be placed on the casing string (e.g. operating annulus

   pressure controlled test tools) must also be taken into account when planning pressure
    tests).
•  Test pressures must not exceed any of the following:
   o  70% of burst pressure of the weakest casing.
   o  Wellhead rated pressure.
   o  BOP rated pressure.
•  Due consideration must be given to the following factors:
   o  The burst rating of the weakest casing in the string.
   o  The density of the mud columns inside and outside the casing.
   o  The minimum design factors assumed in the casing design.
   o  The effect of pressure testing on casing tensile loads.
•  Production casing strings that are to be used in a well for production or injection
   operations must be designed and pressure tested to the maximum possible wellhead
    pressure.
•   Liner overlaps will be positively pressure tested to a minimum of 500 psi over formation
    leak-off pressure of previous casing; meanwhile an inflow test must be carried out, with
   a sufficient drawdown to test the liner top to the most negative differential pressure that
    will exist during the life on the well. The type of fluid below the packer during negative
    differential pressure calculation must be considered as existing drilling fluid in the hole.
•  The test pressure and method for each well are determined on an individual basis.
•  Casing wear and consequent reduction in casing strength must be considered during
   planning of drilling and well testing operations.

18. Well Control Procedure
The PECO Well Control Manual brought into force earlier but not later than commence drilling through
Gachsaran formation with the mutual agreement of the parties. Introducing the PECO Well Control
Manual earlier may be prudent if the formation tops and pore pressures vary significantly from that
forecast.

The PECO Well Control Manual applies to all well operations conducted in the transition zone, and
reservoir sections of the JR-09 well. This includes all drilling and well Completion/Testing activities.

The procedures and practices in the PECO Well Control Manual provide guidance from which specific
procedures are to be developed to take account of the prevailing rig and well conditions. All key
members of PECO, Rig Contractor and appropriate service contractors must review these procedures.

However, for any other Well Control procedures and guidelines to take precedence over the ones
shown in the “PECO Well Control Manual”, the following is a must and cannot be deviated:

1.  At least two tested Safety Barriers shall be present in drilling and producing wells. If for some
    reason only one Safety Barrier is present, all activities shall cease until two Safety Barriers are re-
    established.
2.   All Safety Barriers must be tested in accordance with approved procedures, or as specified in the
   program prepared for the specific operation.
3.  Activity Typical Independent Barriers:
        • Drilling
      A sufficient amount of mud or fluid of adequate density to control the well bore pressure,
         certified and tested BOP stack dressed with suitable rams; unperforated, cemented and
        pressure tested casing or liner; tested downhole plug; back pressure valve (BPV).
        • Casing
      A sufficient amount of mud or fluid of adequate density to control the well bore pressure;
         certified and tested BOP stack dressed with suitable Casing rams.
        • Production
       Christmas tree; surface controlled subsurface safety valve (SCSSV); downhole plug.
        • Wireline
       Christmas tree valves; wireline BOP; wireline lubricator.

18.1.  Well Control Incident Report
The reportable incidents are as follows:
•  When Hydrogen Sulphide (H2S) is detected during operations or samples of well fluid (not
    applicable where H2S is known to be present).
•  When a BOP or diverter is operated to control a flow from a well.
•  When a failure of blowout prevention systems, wellheads or casings, leads to an interruption of
    operations on the well to carry out immediate repairs.

18.2. Kick Indicators/Warning Signs
Primary well control warning signs and early detection is paramount to identify that an alert condition
results, i.e. that a kick may be developing! Every endeavor then taken by all personnel to assure the
following well control risks are managed as low as reasonably practicable e.g.

•   Positive gain in the active mud pit volume
•   In sufficient hole-fill or returns volumes of fluids during tripping
•   Increased flow from annulus
•  Decrease in pump pressure
•   Loss Circulation
•   Losses and gains to/from the wellbore
•   Rapid increase in penetration rate (drilling break)
•  Decrease in penetration rate (inverse drilling break PDC enters a sand)
•  Gas cut mud and/or increase in chloride content in mud
•   Swabbing, especially the "low volume swabbing" and the dangerous effect of migrating and
   expanding gas
•  Unexpected increased readings on gas-chromatograph
•   Trip gas and increased trip gas during sub-sequent round trips
•   Connection gas
•   Pressure caving’s appear on shakers
•   Increasing pump strokes, ROP, torque and drag trends all indicating pore pressure may be
    increasing
•   Flowline temperature increases

When these warning signs occur, an alert condition exists. Immediate action must then be taken to
assure that well control risks can be safely managed at the lowest risk.

18.4. Well Control Procedure in Summary
Personnel
It is required that each member of crew should be familiar with every item of equipment used in well
control. The minimum personal knowledge and capability required for a crew member to be
considered competent are:
•  To have sufficient knowledge of all the equipment in order to be able to determine when
    operating functions are not working properly, and consequently, take all necessary remedial
    actions to re-instate full functionality.
•  To have sufficient knowledge of operating procedures in order to be able to react in time,
    understanding completely what is occurring.
•  To be able to correctly interpret the various abnormal situations and take the appropriate
    remedial steps of action. Carry out basic calculations, and use the results in order to safely manage
   any occurrences.

Key personnel shall have the fundamental theoretical knowledge on kick and blow-out control
techniques and also hold a current Well Control Certificate issued by an accredited industry training
institute recognized by Governmental bodies and operators.

Recordings
All BOP test, drills, function test, any malfunction, repair or maintenance to the mud system and well
control equipment shall be recorded in the IADC daily reports and shall be signed by both the Drilling
Contractor's Tool Pusher and Drilling Supervisor on the well site. They shall also be recorded in the
PECO Daily Drilling Report.

Flow Check Procedure
To avoid a kick situation, it is recommended that a flow check be conducted at specific times during
the drilling operation.
    1.  While drilling (any warning sign)
    2.  Prior to tripping the drill string
    3.  While out of hole (continuously)
    4.  While tripping (any warning sign)
        Trip out:
           •   After pulling 5% of the drill pipe
           •   At the midpoint depth of the wellbore
           •   Prior to pulling the first stand of drill collars
           •   After all the drill string is out of hole.
        Trip in:
           •  Upon reaching surface casing shoe
           •   At midpoint of the wellbore

Killing Well Method and Shut-In Method
•   Driller's method is recommended main killing methods for the project.
•  The hard shut-in method is recommended to minimize influx.

Kick detection and Hard Shut in Procedure While Drilling
• Kick detection procedure:
If there  is an indication of a possible kick occurring, the driller shall follow the kick detection
procedures outlined below.
a) Stop drilling, pick up drill pipe to a predetermined Space-out position with pump on.
b) Shut off pump and check for well flow by visual examination on the bell nipple, flow line and mud
pit.
           If the well is not flowing to be confirmed:
       Immediately notify the drilling supervisor and toolpusher.
      The Drilling Supervisor will decide whether to circulate bottoms up or resume drilling. The
       penetration rate  will be limited as long as the cause of the abnormal  situation  is
       undetermined. Always be aware that some hydrocarbons (gas or oil cut mud) may rise to the
        surface. Ensure that the proper monitoring and safety systems all in place.

           If the well is flowing to be confirmed:
       Close the well as per the Hard Shut-in Procedure.

• Hard Shut-in Procedure
a)  Space kelly (if in use) and/or tool joint so that tool joints are clear of sealing elements.
b) Pump off and flow check.
c)   If a kick is confirmed, sound alarm.
d)  Close annular preventer and open remote controlled choke line valve (HCR).
e)   If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out (pipe rams vs. toll joint
    relative position) and close pipe rams and ram locks
f)  Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (if possible).
g)  Record shut-in drill pipe pressure and shut-in casing pressures.
h)  Record volume gain and mark pits.
i)  Check mud weight for in and out.
j)  Check blowout preventer and manifold for leaks.
k)  Check flowline and choke exhaust for flow.
l)  Check accumulator pressure.

Kick Detection and Hard Shut in Procedure while Tripping
• Kick Detection Procedure
If there  is an indication of a possible kick occurring, the driller shall follow the kick detection
procedures outlined below.
a) Stop tripping; slack off string to a predetermined space-out position.
b) Install a fully open safety valve and hand tight on drill pipe/work string. Close the safety valve.
c) Check for well flow by visual examination on the bell nipple, flow line and mud pit.

           If the well is not flowing to be confirmed:
      Resume tripping with extreme care.

           If the well is flowing to be confirmed:
       Close the well as per the Hard Shut-In Procedure

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
                 Sepehr-Jufair Field Development and Production
                             Operations Project

                                  Well Drilling Program - JR-09

 Doc. No:            SJD4   DDRGED   DRDR    PLDR     9001     D01      Page 278 of 281

• Hard Shut-in Procedure
a)   If a kick is confirmed, sound alarm.
b)  Install full opened safety valve on drill string and close same.
c)  Space tool joints clear of sealing elements and close annular preventer. Open remote controlled
   choke line valve (HCR).
d) Make up kelly or top drive (Add a pup joint or single between safety valve and top drive). Open
    safety valve.
e)  Record shut-in drill pipe pressure and shut-in casing pressures.
f)  Check blowout preventer, stack, and manifold for leaks. Check valves status on well control
    system. Check accumulator pressure.
g)  Check mud weight for in and out..
h) Manage to strip to bottom.

Kick Detection and Hard Shut in Procedure while Out of Hole
• Kick Detection Procedure
If there  is an indication of a possible kick occurring, the driller shall follow the kick detection
procedures outlined below.
a) Stop working immediately.
b) Check for well flowing by visual examination on the bell nipple, flow line and mud pit.

           If the well is not flowing to be confirmed:
      Resume working and continuously monitoring well.

           If the well is flowing to be confirmed:
       Close the well as per the ‗Hard Shut-In Procedure‘

• Hard Shut-in Procedure
a)  Manage to RIH with drill pipe as more as possible if hole condition permits, and the drill pipe must
   be installed a full opening safety valve (stabbing valve).
b)  Close the annular preventer and open remote controlled choke line valve (HCR).
c)   If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out (pipe rams vs. toll joint
    relative position) and close pipe rams and ram locks.
d)  Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (if possible).
e)  Record shut-in drill pipe pressure and shut-in casing pressures.

Well Control During Running Casing
The well control while running casing is important and critical, best practices shall be followed,
including but not limited to:
Change out pipe size rams with casing size rams prior to running casing for expected hydrocarbon
bearing formation, if possible except running a liner string with drill pipe.
The crossover for casing connection to drill pipe must available on floor. A good practice is to keep a
joint of DP with casing crossover at lower end and full opened safety valve at upper end to be ready
for picking up on V-door.

Shut in procedure during logging
Recover logging tools as possible when a kick is suspected during logging. If pit gain exceeds the
specified amount, Wire line should be cut immediately. Sound alarm and shut in well as procedure for
empty wells. Recover cable through closed annular preventer is not recommended.
